title: Incremental Assertion Protocol and Client Handoff — PRD draft
content:
Purpose
This is a working PRD for an Incremental Assertion Protocol (IAP) and a client handoff pattern for the Hosted API streaming surface. The goal is to make structured assertions (partial results, tool calls, validation events) first-class, resumable, and ergonomically accessible from SDKs while minimizing bandwidth and client parsing work.

Context / Problem
- Current streaming outputs are free-form text with ad-hoc JSON blobs for structured outputs. That causes client parsing complexity and brittle heuristics when resuming or when interleaving tool calls.
- Tool calls and their results are treated as separate events without a stable, resumable identity. If a connection drops the client must either re-run prompts or accept potential duplication.
- Mobile and low-bandwidth clients struggle to maintain long-lived streams and want smaller, checkpointed updates.
- SDK ergonomics are inconsistent: some SDKs expose raw frames, others try to parse and convert to high-level objects leading to duplication of parsing logic.

Goals
1) Define a compact streaming frame protocol that explicitly encodes: assertion fragments, commit checkpoints, tool call intents, tool results, and resumable tokens.
2) Make tool calls idempotent and resumable from the client perspective (no duplicate external side-effects if the client reconnects).
3) Provide SDK-level primitives that are strongly typed (language-level) and optimized for lazy parsing so clients can avoid materializing full transcripts.
4) Low-bandwidth friendliness: allow clients to request lower-fidelity frames (assertion summaries vs full assertions).
5) Observability: surface assertion-level telemetry (which assertions committed, rejected, latency to commit, tool call success rate).

Non-goals
- This PRD does NOT attempt to design a full schema registry for arbitrary structured outputs (that may follow). Focus is on a small assertion envelope and compositor.
- Not designing server-side routing policies for model variants; assume current routing stacks.

User stories
- As a mobile app developer, I want to reconnect after a network failure and resume the chat without duplicated API-side tool calls.
- As a backend engineer, I want per-assertion traces so I can correlate a mis-generated action with the model input that produced it.
- As an SDK user, I want a callback that receives typed assertion objects as they commit, not raw text diffs.
- As an enterprise security admin, I want to ensure tool calls performed via Hosted API are recorded with idempotency keys and auditable metadata.

High-level protocol (IAP)
- Frame types: ASSERT, PATCH, COMMIT, CHECKPOINT, TOOL_CALL, TOOL_RESULT, HEARTBEAT, RESUME_REQUEST, RESUME_RESPONSE, ERROR.
- ASSERT: incremental semantic assertions. Contains assertion_id, parent_assertion_id (optional), delta (small JSON-LD-like fragment), confidence, optional schema pointer.
- PATCH: lightweight text/semantic patch to a previous ASSERT (used only for small corrections).
- COMMIT: marks that an assertion is stable and can be acted upon (e.g., trigger a tool). Contains commit_token usable for resumability and deduping.
- CHECKPOINT: periodic durable snapshot of session state (sequence number, last_commit_token, optional KV hash for fast validation on resume).
- TOOL_CALL: intent envelope emitted by server or client to declare a tool invocation. Contains tool_id, call_id, params_ref (may be inline or a content-hash reference), idempotency_key, requested_behavior (sync/async). The Hosted API will guarantee at-least-once execution but provide mechanisms to allow clients detect duplicates via call_id + idempotency_key.
- TOOL_RESULT: result envelope with call_id, status, result_ref, and commit_token if the result is persisted.
- RESUME_REQUEST / RESPONSE: used by clients reconnecting; client sends last_known_sequence/checkpoint; server responds with minimal delta stream and a new resume token.

Example sequence
1) ASSERT(a1: "User asked to schedule meeting")
2) ASSERT(a2: "Suggested time slot: Thu 3-4pm" parent=a1)
3) COMMIT(token=t1 for a2) -> SDK triggers onCommit(a2, t1)
4) TOOL_CALL(call_id=c1, tool_id=calendar.create, params_ref=hash://xyz, idempotency=key1)
5) TOOL_RESULT(call_id=c1, status=ok, result_ref=hash://abc)
6) COMMIT(token=t2 for TOOL_RESULT(c1))
7) CHECKPOINT(seq=42, last_commit=t2)

Resumability guarantees (server-side contract suggestion)
- Server stores commit tokens + tool call states for a TTL (configurable by account/plan).
- When client resumes with checkpoint seq=42, server replays only frames after seq=42. For any TOOL_CALLs whose call_id already completed, server re-emits TOOL_RESULT frames (not re-execute the tool).
- If server cannot honor resume (state evicted), it responds with RESUME_RESPONSE{reset:true} and client will have to reconcile by re-sending high-level context.

Idempotency model for tool calls
- Primary dedupe key = (call_id, idempotency_key). call_id assigned by server when it initiates; if client initiates a tool call, client can suggest call_id but server may canonicalize.
- Server will persist the side-effecting outcome and associate it with call_id + commit_token. On resume, server returns the TOOL_RESULT rather than re-executing.

SDK ergonomics proposals
- High-level SDK surfaces across languages (JS, Python, Java, Go):
  - Session.start(params) -> Session object with stream() and checkpoint() helpers.
  - Session.on('assertion', handler(assertion)) where assertion is a small typed object with assertion.id, type, payload_ref, confidence, commit(token).
  - Session.on('tool_call', handler(callContext)) where handler can answer with callAction.accept()/decline() and optionally provide params. Alternatively, provide declarative handlers: registerToolHandler(tool_id, fn).
  - Lazy payload access: assertion.payload is a lazy accessor: .get() returns parsed structure only when needed, and .summary() returns a 1-2 sentence summary extracted by server.
  - Checkpoint API: session.checkpoint() returns a human-friendly resume token; session.resume(token) resumes existing Session object.
  - Opt-in small-frame mode: session.withFidelity('summary' | 'full') controls server fidelity. Mobile clients default to 'summary'.
  - Fail-fast mode for tools: registerToolHandler(tool_id, { idempotent: true, allowReplay: false }) to control client-side behavior when uncertain about duplication. SDK will expose metadata for tool calls (call_id, idempotency_key, committed_at).

Wire-size and low-bandwidth considerations
- Use short numeric frame types and base64- or protobuf-encoded payload bodies for compactness.
- Server-sent 'summary' field for assertions to avoid sending full payloads unless client requests.
- Allow offloading full payloads to blob storage (content-hash references) so clients can fetch on-demand over HTTP with caching.

Observability / Telemetry
- Emit metrics: assertions_committed_total, assertion_commit_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, tool_call_invocations_total, tool_call_duplicate_count, resume_success_rate, average_frames_per_session.
- Trace spans per-assertion that include model_version, sequence_id, commit_token, tool_call_ids referenced.
- Exposure in Console: per-session timeline view with checkboxes for committed vs tentative assertions and a toggle to view full payloads vs summaries.

Compatibility and migration
- Backwards compatibility: Existing clients that only expect text will still receive a TEXT_FRAME wrapper (server will emit a TEXT frame for backward compatibility). New clients can negotiate using an Alpn-like header or initial capability frame to request IAP.
- Opt-in rollout: default to opt-out (clients must request iap=true in session.start). Plan a migration: alpha with internal apps -> early access customers -> open beta.

Security and compliance
- Tool_call idempotency keys and commit_tokens should be logged with minimal PI in audit logs. Provide an option for customers to disable tool persistence if their compliance requirements forbid server-side storage of PII.
- Signed resume tokens for tamper-evidence (HMAC per-account key). Document retention policy for resume state.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Schema pointers vs inline small JSON: do we require a lightweight schema registry? (pros: validated payloads; cons: higher ops).
- TTL defaults for resume state by plan tier (30m for free, 7d for enterprise?).
- Do we provide server-side automatic idempotency_key generation for client-originated tool calls or require client-provided keys? Hybrid approach seems safest.
- How to model multi-turn tool transactions that require multiple tool calls (saga-like semantics). Add guardrails in SDK?

Rollout plan / milestones (rough)
- Week 0-3: finalize frame spec, implement minimal server wire parser and stubbed resume store (in-memory for alpha). SDK minimal JS + Python prototypes.
- Week 4-6: internal dogfood with Conversations and Console teams, add tooling to visualize per-assertion timeline.
- Week 7-10: limited alpha with 3 external customers (mobile chat, scheduling integration, customer success triage bot).
- Week 11-14: incorporate feedback, add robust persistence, security review, and beta docs.

Success metrics (initial)
- Reduce duplicate tool invocations on resume to <1% in alpha customers.
- Achieve resume_success_rate >= 98% for sessions where server state not evicted.
- Reduce mobile bandwidth for typical session by 35% when fidelity='summary'.

Open TODOs (author notes)
- [ ] Draft protobuf/compact binary encoding for frames (ENG-1259)
- [ ] Prototype JS lazy payload accessor and benchmark memory usage (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/432)
- [ ] Define retention policy per plan (Product + Legal)
- [ ] Add console timeline mockups (Design owns)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight on schema choices; want to get the envelope right first and iterate on payload schemas.
- Look for gaps in the resumability guarantees and any edge cases where tool external side-effects might be duplicated.

-- end of draft --

References and contextual links (copied for reviewer convenience)
- internal convo: slack:#hosted-api-proto thread 12345
- related PRD: https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/HOST/Streaming+Tooling+Playbook

Feedback requested by 2025-02-10: priority on deciding TTL defaults and idempotency model.
